newsitem.title: ITALY: Germany wants no EMU discount, delay - CDU's Lamers.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants no EMU discount, delay - CDU's Lamers.

text.p: Germany believes European economic and monetary union will be launched on time in 1999 and is not seeking any special treatment, a senior member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrat party said on Monday.
"We will fulfil the criteria. There will be no flexible interpretation, I do not like the word flexible," Karl Lamers, the CDU's foreign policy spokesman, told a conference in Rome.
He said there was "no more room for postponement" for the launch of Europe's single currency set for January 1, 1999.
Lamers said Germany "would never agree to a weakening of the key 3.0 (percent deficit to gross domestic product ratio)" set as the target ceiling for entry into the single currency.
But he added: "In the end the decision will not be a question of 3.0 percent or 2.8 percent. The decisive question is that of sustainability."

Germany, battling to shore up public finances, last week announced plans to revalue gold reserves, prompting an outcry that Europe's economic powerhouse was itself bending accounting methods to make sure it qualified for EMU.

Lamers praised Italy's strenuous efforts to qualify, although the political climate in Germany has been more sceptical, believing Rome's history of political and financial instability would weaken the planned single currency, the euro.
"I recognise what has been done in the last few years. I know how difficult it has been and I hope that my compatriots also understand it," Lamers said.

Massimo D'Alema, whose Democratic Party of the Left is the biggest in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government, told Reuters Financial Television in an interview that he expected Italy to be in the first wave of EMU entrants.

"If (exclusion) resulted from the fact that we do not make the grade, we won't be able to complain. But if, on the other hand, we were prevented, that would not be fair. In any case, I do not believe we will be excluded," he said.
